items.title: [codex] standardize evaluation protocols
items.body:
## What changed

- Restrict public evaluation summaries and paper exports to audited `standard_*` metrics.
- Delegate Global Grasp benchmarking to the official GraspNet evaluator.
- Add executed VPG episode and Task Grasp success evaluation.
- Remove legacy known-pose Global Grasp evaluator modules and CLI entry point.
- Add protocol documentation, audit enforcement, and regression coverage.

## Why

The previous evaluation surface exposed TCD-specific proxy metrics alongside externally comparable results. This made it possible to report numbers whose protocol did not match the cited benchmarks.

This change follows a conservative standard-only policy: when the available labels cannot implement an accepted protocol, no substitute public metric is emitted.

## Compatibility fixes

- Updated stale tests that imported the removed evaluator or expected removed policy proxy metrics.
- Updated the root README to use the official GraspNet evaluation entry point.
- Kept legacy configuration fields loadable where needed, without exporting legacy metrics.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest -q` with third-party pytest plugin autoload disabled: 152 passed.
- Focused protocol tests: 8 passed.
- Ruff checks passed for all changed evaluation and test files.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- New console entry points were installed and smoke-tested; the legacy command is absent.

items.title: Add model-adapter contract and COMPASS feasibility gate
items.body:
## Summary

- finalise the shared capability metadata required for accepting model adapters
- strengthen the production `ScoreResult` with canonical unit codes, typed provenance, result classification, validation evidence, limitations, warnings, and comparability metadata
- add a fail-closed `ModelAdapter` contract that checks request capabilities and request/result correspondence
- migrate the real PolicyEngine-to-OBR bridge as the first adapter-template implementation
- add reusable contract tests and a contributor acceptance checklist
- document the Bank of England COMPASS feasibility review with a no-go decision until code, licensing, complete inputs, and numerical benchmarks become available

## Why

Issue #71 identified that new models must not become bespoke integrations. The earlier draft contract created a parallel result envelope and did not ensure that returned results matched their requests. This version uses the existing production result type and rejects mismatched models, geography, baselines, horizons, outputs, provenance, timestamps, and unknown adapter inputs.

## Impact

Contributors now have one documented integration boundary and checklist. COMPASS is not implemented or represented as reproducible; its reconsideration conditions are explicit.

## Verification

- `156 passed, 62 skipped`
- `git diff --check`

Addresses #71.

items.title: Correct inflated benchmark numbers in docs to match results JSON
items.body:
## Why

A post-project audit found that several **headline numbers in the public docs did not match the actual benchmark outputs** in `results/*.json`. The benchmark *machinery* (token counts, latency, correctness, cost-arithmetic) is real and computed on the real 200-pair / 200-tuple datasets — but the hand-written prose in README and SYSTEM_WRITEUP had drifted to inflated values. This PR reconciles every doc to the data.

Notably, the project's own designated source-of-truth (`ui/demo_scenario.py` `PHASE_FINDINGS` dict) and `docs/POLICIES.md` were already accurate — only the narrative prose had drifted.

## Corrections (claimed → actual, from results JSON)

| Doc claim | Actual value (results file) |
|---|---|
| naive 12,800 / hybrid 2,480 tokens | **1,449.6 / 838.4** (`phase3_day18_consolidated`) |
| hybrid "~6× cheaper" | **24% cheaper** ($0.585 vs $0.769; `phase5_*`) |
| hybrid "3× faster" | **slightly slower** (0.48 ms vs 0.24 ms p50) |
| quality 4.1 / 4.2, "goes up" | **tied 3.9/5** fact-subset; Phase-3 mock-proxy 3.04 vs hybrid 2.91 |
| naive-LLM "~11 ms" latency | **1.8 µs** (mock-mode local compute) |
| policy "~17,000× cheaper" | **$0 vs ~$0.57/100 projected** (undefined ratio — removed) |

## What's now stated honestly

- A **Measurement honesty** note in README + SYSTEM_WRITEUP: the whole project ran in `MOCK_LLM` mode; quality is a **mock-proxy token-overlap heuristic**, not a real LLM judge; policy-engine latencies are **local compute** (no network).
- The real, defensible findings kept: hybrid uses **42% fewer tokens** at parity recall (183/200), **24% cheaper** at tied quality; declarative **100% vs naive-LLM 54%** correctness at **zero marginal cost**, naive-LLM misses all 5 reject scenarios.

## Files
- `README.md`, `docs/SYSTEM_WRITEUP.md`, `docs/DEMO_VIDEO_SCRIPT.md`, `context_engine/README.md`, `orchestrator/README.md`, `results/metrics.json`
- (`docs/POLICIES.md`, `ui/`, `SYSTEM_DESIGN.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` were already accurate — unchanged.)

Tests unaffected (docs-only): suite stays 871 passed / 10 skipped / 90% coverage.

items.title: docs(readme): refresh result tables from RUNS=5 run; drop stale claims
items.body:
Re-run of the full arena (`RUNS=5`, gate green — 434 B / 494 B on all 18 targets) moves every throughput figure and the `rust-cortex-m` / `rust-riscv` footprints. This refreshes `results/RESULTS.txt` and hand-syncs the three README tables from it, per the "README tables are hand-refreshed after a full RUNS=5 run" rule.

## The numbers moved enough to falsify three claims in the prose

| claim | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| "Zig, C++, Rust, C#, Go **and Java** all beat protobuf" | Java 1.02× | **Java 0.85×** — dropped from the list |
| "Zig by 2.3×" | 2.32× | **1.86×** |
| "~3× vs EmbeddedProto" | 3.07× | **2.32×** — caption now "~2× vs both" |

The big-picture bullet said Java and TypeScript "land around parity"; at 0.85×/0.65× that no longer holds, so it now reads "land modestly behind (0.85×/0.65×)". The bare-metal footprint ratio range also narrows from 1.43×–2.02× to **1.34×–1.94×** — SofaBuffers still wins all six bare-metal rows.

## Worth a reviewer's eye

The README footprint table was stale by **more than this run**: its sofab figures (e.g. `cpp-cortex-m` 6 504) did not match even the *committed* `RESULTS.txt` (6 952). Those predate the sofabgen v0.17.3 bump in 609da1d, which explicitly traded footprint for speed — so that commit moved the results file but not the README. This PR closes both gaps at once, which is why the footprint deltas look larger than one re-run would explain.

## Also included

`languages/typescript/sofab/gen/package-lock.json` — the regenerated lockfile (tsx 4.23.1) that `setup.sh` reconciles with the `versions.sh` bump merged in 11443f2. It is a generated manifest that the benchmark run updated; excluding it would leave the tree dirty and re-appear on the next run.

## Verification

- Gate: `434B ok` / `494B ok` on every target; all 18 report `OK`.
- Best-of-5 confirmed from `results/raw/` (5 BENCH lines per impl, per target).
- No schema, generator, or reference-wire change — the wire is untouched at 434 B / 494 B, so no sync-point update is needed.

items.title: fix(desktop): harden Windows screen publication recovery
items.body: ## Summary - Rebuilds the Windows H.264 Media Foundation encoder selection around adapter-aware capability checks and fully validates each candidate before it can be used. - Separates encoder stalls from transport stalls, adds bounded recovery with typed terminal failures, and closes generation-fence races that could leave screen sharing oscillating or silently stuck. - Makes camera frame ingestion safe for legacy Media Foundation buffers by validating stride, length, and arithmetic before copying. - Preserves fatal diagnostic state and applies the configured supervisor restart schedule consistently. ## Root cause The stable reports showed frames reaching native capture while the encoder produced no access units. The publication pipeline treated partial Media Foundation initialization as success, accepted unsupported codec-control results, and did not verify that the encoder matched the active D3D11 adapter. Recovery then mixed encoder and transport failures, retried without a bounded terminal state, and could race stale generations. The changes make those contracts explicit from capture ingress through encoder startup, publication recovery, diagnostics, and shutdown. ## Validation - `pnpm desktop-native:build` - `pnpm desktop-native:test` — 17/17 native tests and 2/2 smoke tests - `pnpm desktop:test` — 31 files, 275/275 tests - `pnpm desktop:typecheck` - `pnpm desktop-native:verify` - Production web build and verification - NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti hardware benchmark: 60 inputs produced 60 H.264 access units, including forced/late-join keyframes, with clean shutdown and tracked input lifetime - Real DXGI capture through an NV12 shared texture and GPU preview - Nightly NSIS package build and verification Relates to #50 --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved camera frame handling to prevent invalid or truncated media buffers from causing failures. * Enhanced screen sharing recovery for encoder and network stalls, with clearer failure reporting and bounded retry behavior. * Improved hardware encoder selection and monitoring on Windows. * Corrected frame acceptance reporting during video capture. * Refined voice error diagnostics so fatal and non-fatal events are classified accurately. * Restart handling now uses all configured retry delays before opening the crash circuit.

items.title: feat(benchmarks): harness comparing engine vs Naive vs Matrix Profile
items.body:
## Summary
- New `benchmarks/` package: dataset loaders (M4 Daily/Hourly, NN5 Daily, SPY Daily), system adapters (`SeasonalNaive`, `MatrixProfile` via STUMPY, `TheSimilarity` engine at default `Config()`), metric suite (MAE, sMAPE, CRPS, MASE, coverage_p10_p90), and a Cartesian sweep runner with resume support that emits one JSONL line per `(dataset, series_id, system, horizon)`.
- 19 new tests (`the_similarity/tests/test_benchmarks.py`): hand-computed metric checks, deterministic naive checks on a sawtooth, MP smoke (auto-skip when STUMPY unavailable), engine smoke, runner end-to-end + resume regression. **All 1,260 repo tests pass under `bash scripts/ci_local.sh`.**
- Smoke `benchmarks/results/raw.jsonl` (6 rows from a small synthetic sinusoidal dataset) committed so Agent B's report layer has fixtures to develop against immediately.

## Honesty constraints (per task spec)
- **No tuning.** Every system runs at its library default config; the engine adapter calls `the_similarity.api.search()` and `project()` with `Config()` (no overrides).
- **Default M4 cap = 100 series per frequency** (deterministic seed=42 sample).
- **Resume-aware runner** so the user can interrupt long sweeps without losing progress.
- **No new pyproject.toml deps.** Loaders use `urllib` + `csv` + `pandas` (already in pyproject). STUMPY is treated as an OPTIONAL dependency: `benchmarks/systems/__init__.py` registers `MatrixProfile` only when `import stumpy` succeeds (catches both `ImportError` and `OSError` because numba/llvmlite raise `OSError` on macOS when the native lib can't load). Users who want the matrix-profile baseline run `pip install stumpy` separately.
- **No Chronos dependency** — Agent B handles published-paper numbers.
- **Did not edit the repo `.gitignore`** because of the existing `<<<<<<< HEAD ... >>>>>>> origin/main` conflict markers there (the parallel-agent rules in `CLAUDE.md` say "only one agent per batch should touch it"). Cache + result outputs are gitignored via `benchmarks/cache/.gitignore` and `benchmarks/results/.gitignore` instead.
- **Did not touch `obsidian_thesim/_MOC.md`.**

## Output schema (matches what Agent B expects)
```json
{"dataset": "m4_daily", "series_id": "D1", "system": "engine",
 "horizon": 5, "mae": 12.3, "smape": 8.4, "crps": 0.04,
 "mase": 1.21, "coverage_p10_p90": 0.79,
 "query_ms": 1.2, "peak_mb": 0.4}
```

## Run the full sweep (user does this locally)
```bash
python -m benchmarks.runners.run --datasets all --systems all --horizons 5,20
# Output: benchmarks/results/raw.jsonl (resume-aware)
```

## Test plan
- [x] `python -m pytest the_similarity/tests/test_benchmarks.py -v` → 18 passed, 1 skipped (STUMPY missing locally).
- [x] `bash scripts/ci_local.sh` → 1,260 passed, 5 skipped.
- [x] `ruff check the_similarity/ benchmarks/` → all clean.
- [ ] User runs the full M4 + NN5 + SPY sweep locally and shares `raw.jsonl` with Agent B for the report markdown.

items.title: Documentation: Fix Performance Metrics Accuracy
items.body:
## Problem

README.md contained performance metrics that did not match the actual benchmark results documented in BASELINE.md, creating reproducibility and credibility issues.

### Specific Discrepancies Found

1. **Benchmark Environment Mismatch**
   - README claimed: Intel i7-12700K, Windows 11, MSVC 2022
   - Actual (BASELINE.md): Apple M1, macOS 26.1, Apple Clang 17.0
   - Impact: Cross-platform confusion, cannot reproduce claimed results

2. **Serialization Performance Inaccuracies**
   - JSON: README 400K/s vs BASELINE 950K/s (137% understatement)
   - XML: README 200K/s vs BASELINE 720K/s (260% understatement)
   - MessagePack: README 1.8M/s vs BASELINE 1.6M/s (12.5% overstatement)
   - Binary: README 2M/s vs BASELINE 1.8M/s (11% overstatement)

3. **Memory Usage Misleading**
   - README claimed: ~128 bytes baseline
   - Actual (BASELINE.md): 1.5 MB baseline (empty container)
   - Impact: 11,700x discrepancy, no explanation of measurement conditions

4. **Unverifiable Protocol Buffers Claims**
   - README: 1.2M/s with ~15% overhead
   - Source: No benchmark data exists in repository
   - PERFORMANCE.md references different units (MB/s not ops/s)

## Solution

### Changes Made

1. **Corrected Benchmark Environment**
   ```
   - Before: Intel i7-12700K (16 threads) @ 3.8GHz, Windows 11, MSVC 2022
   + After: Apple M1 (8 cores, ARM NEON), macOS 26.1, Apple Clang 17.0
   ```
   Added disclaimer: "Performance metrics are platform-dependent"

2. **Updated Serialization Metrics to Match BASELINE.md**
   | Metric | README (Before) | BASELINE.md (Actual) | README (After) |
   |--------|----------------|----------------------|----------------|
   | Binary | 2M/s | 1.8M ops/s | 1.8M ops/s ✓ |
   | JSON | 400K/s | 950K ops/s | 950K ops/s ✓ |
   | XML | 200K/s | 720K ops/s | 720K ops/s ✓ |
   | MessagePack | 1.8M/s | 1.6M ops/s | 1.6M ops/s ✓ |

3. **Fixed Memory Baseline**
   ```
   - Before: ~128 bytes baseline with optimized variant storage
   + After: 1.5 MB (empty container with allocator overhead)
   ```

4. **Updated SIMD Performance**
   ```
   - Before: 2.5x performance boost
   + After: 3.2x performance boost (scalar: 1.2 GB/s → NEON: 3.8 GB/s)
   ```
   Source: BASELINE.md Table 5

5. **Removed Unverifiable Protocol Buffers Comparison**
   - Replaced with note: "Direct comparison requires identical data structures and measurement methodology"
   - Added reference: "See benchmarks/protobuf_comparison.md (when available)"

6. **Added Scalability Data**
   Performance degradation with container size (from BASELINE.md):
   - 10 values: 3.5M ops/s
   - 100 values: 2.0M ops/s
   - 1000 values: 450K ops/s

### Documentation Consistency

- ✅ README.md matches BASELINE.md data
- ✅ README_KO.md matches BASELINE.md data
- ✅ Performance comparison table uses consistent units (ops/s)
- ✅ Platform disclaimers added to prevent confusion
- ✅ References to BASELINE.md and PERFORMANCE.md for details

## Impact

### Before (Issues)
- ❌ Claims could not be reproduced (wrong platform)
- ❌ JSON/XML performance significantly understated
- ❌ Memory usage claim 11,700x off
- ❌ Protocol Buffers comparison unverifiable
- ❌ No mention of performance scaling characteristics

### After (Fixed)
- ✅ All metrics match measured BASELINE.md results
- ✅ Platform clearly identified (Apple M1)
- ✅ Disclaimer added for cross-platform differences
- ✅ Memory usage accurate with explanation
- ✅ Unverifiable claims removed or qualified
- ✅ Scalability characteristics documented

## Verification

All metrics verified against:
- Primary source: `BASELINE.md` lines 41-70
- Cross-reference: `BASELINE_KO.md`
- Platform info: `BASELINE.md` lines 14-26

## Files Modified

- `README.md` - English documentation
- `README_KO.md` - Korean documentation

## Breaking Changes

None. This is purely documentation correction.

## Recommendations for Future

1. Add automated script to extract metrics from BASELINE.md into README
2. Create benchmarks/protobuf_comparison.md with controlled comparison
3. Add CI check to ensure README metrics match BASELINE.md
4. Consider adding Windows/x86 benchmark results as separate section

## Related Issues

Addresses documentation accuracy concerns raised in code review.
